 Wisconsin DMV extends hours ahead of Election Day 
 By WBAY news staff Published : Nov. 2, 2026 at 8:17 PM CST | Updated : 12 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google GREEN BAY, Wis. (WBAY) - The Wisconsin Department of Transportation (WisDOT) Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV) will extend hours at customer service centers on Monday, Nov. 2, and Tuesday, Nov. 3 (Election Day). 
 Service centers will remain open until 6 p.m. both days. The extended hours give people who need a photo ID time to visit a DMV.
 Who can get an ID
 Voters who don’t already have a Wisconsin driver license, ID or other form of identification needed to vote may still get a Wisconsin ID from the DMV. The Wisconsin Elections Commission website explains the options for IDs to show at the polls.
 There is no separate “voter ID.” A federally compliant REAL ID card is not required for voting.
 Documents and process
 Documentation requirements to get an official Wisconsin ID card include a birth certificate, proof of identity and Wisconsin residency. Voters should bring any documentation available to the DMV and fill out two forms. The DMV’s new Find My DMV locator helps customers find a site.
 A photo ID document will be sent by overnight mail. It may be taken to the polls and used for voting. Completing a provisional ballot may be an option until the photo ID document arrives.
 Cost and contact information
 The DMV offers ID cards for voting purposes to U.S. citizens free of charge. The DMV’s toll-free hotline, (844) 588-1069, is available for questions about getting an ID for voting.
 Questions about voter eligibility, poll locations, voter registration or other election information may be answered on the Wisconsin Elections Commission website, elections.wi.gov.
